t.4.37.1: And having accepted all the gifts that had been brought to him, and having spoken kindly to the vānaras, he dismissed every one of them.
t.4.37.2: Having dismissed those heroic monkeys who had accomplished their task, he considered himself, and also the mighty Rāghava, to have attained their purpose.
t.4.37.4: Having heard those well-spoken words of Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, supremely delighted, spoke these words.
t.4.37.3: Then Lakṣmaṇa, gladdening Sugrīva, the best of all monkeys and of formidable strength, spoke to him these courteous words: “Come forth from Kiṣkindhā, O gentle one, if it pleases you.”
t.4.37.5: "So be it, let us go; I must abide by your command." Having spoken thus to Lakṣmaṇa, who bore auspicious marks, Sugrīva
t.4.37.6: Then Sugrīva dismissed Tārā and the other women, and called out loudly to the foremost of the monkeys, "Come!"
t.4.37.7: Hearing those words of his, the monkeys came swiftly, all of them with joined palms, those who were fit to look upon women.
t.4.37.8: Then the king, whose splendor was like that of the sun, spoke to those who had arrived: "O monkeys, quickly bring my palanquin here!"
t.4.37.9: Hearing his words, the swift-striding monkeys brought forward a palanquin that was lovely to behold.
t.4.37.10: Seeing that palanquin brought before him, the lord of the monkeys said to Saumitri, "Lakṣmaṇa, let it be mounted quickly."
t.4.37.11: Having spoken thus, Sugrīva, together with Lakṣmaṇa, mounted a golden palanquin, radiant as the sun and borne by mighty monkeys.
t.4.37.13: Hailed with the blare of conches and kettledrums and praised by the bards, Sugrīva set forth, having attained the unsurpassed splendour of kingship.
t.4.37.12: With a white parasol held over his head, and white yak-tail fans being waved on every side.
t.4.37.14: Surrounded by many hundreds of fierce monkeys with weapons in their hands, he went to the place where Rāma was stationed.
t.4.37.15: Having reached that excellent place frequented by Rāma, he of great splendour, together with Lakṣmaṇa, descended from the palanquin.
t.4.37.16: Then, having approached Rāma, he stood with his palms joined in reverence; and as he stood thus with joined palms, the monkeys too did likewise.
t.4.37.17: Seeing that great army of monkeys, which looked like a lake full of budding lotuses, Rāma became well pleased with Sugrīva.
t.4.37.18: Raising up that lord of the monkeys, who had fallen with his head at his feet, Rāghava embraced him with affection and with great respect.
t.4.37.19: Having embraced him, the righteous-souled one then said, "Sit down." Then, seeing him seated on the ground, Rāma spoke these words.
t.4.37.21: But he who abandons dharma and likewise artha and devotes himself to kāma alone is like one who falls asleep at the top of a tree: he wakes only when he has fallen.
t.4.37.20: But he who, always apportioning them rightly, pursues righteousness, wealth, and pleasure each at its proper time, O hero, he is truly a king, O best of monkeys.
t.4.37.22: A king who is intent on slaying his enemies, who delights in winning over and gathering his friends, and who enjoys the fruits of the three aims of life is united with dharma.
t.4.37.24: Thus addressed, Sugrīva spoke these words to Rāma.
t.4.37.23: This time for undertaking the enterprise has now arrived, O destroyer of enemies; so let it be carefully considered, O lord of the tawny ones, together with the monkeys who are your counsellors.
t.4.37.25: My fortune and my fame, and the everlasting kingdom of the monkeys, had been lost. By your grace, O mighty-armed one, all this has been regained by me.
t.4.37.27: O destroyer of foes, these mighty chiefs of the monkeys have arrived by hundreds, bringing with them all the monkeys on the earth.
t.4.37.26: Through your grace, O lord, and through that of your brother, O best of victors, this has come about; whoever does not repay a kindness done to him is a disgrace among men.
t.4.37.28: And bears too, O Rāghava, alert and valiant, and golāṅgūlas, terrible to behold, who know the wildernesses, forests and impassable places.
t.4.37.29: And the monkeys who are sons of gods and Gandharvas, able to take any form at will, are on the road, O Rāghava, each surrounded by his own troops.
t.4.37.30: O scorcher of foes, the heroic monkeys have come, surrounded by hundreds, by hundreds of thousands, by tens of thousands, by crores and by śaṅkus of followers.
t.4.37.31: The vānaras, monkeys and leaders of monkey troops, came in arbudas and hundreds of arbudas, in madhyas and antas, in samudras and parārdhas.
t.4.37.32: They will come, O king, those monkeys equal in valour to the great Indra, resembling Meru and Mandara, who have made their dwellings on the Vindhya and on Meru.
t.4.37.33: They will come to you, those who, having slain the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa together with his kinsmen in battle, will bring back Maithilī.
t.4.37.34: Then, beholding that exertion of the foremost hero among the monkeys, who abided by his command, the wise son of the lord of the earth became, out of joy, like a fully blossomed blue lotus in appearance.
